Mom stays on the phone with her, sometimes for an hour, until she gets home

turns.text: Okay. Lucia, Mom, thanks for coming in. I've got the log here. Lucia, I'd like to hear from you first today, and then we'll bring Mom in. Is that okay?
Yeah, sure.
So the weekend at your grandparents'. What happened?
Friday was fine-ish. I FaceTimed Mom at night and kind of fell asleep on it. Then Saturday I just felt really bad. Like my stomach. And I texted her to come get me.
And how was your stomach in the car on the way home?
Fine. I know. I know how that sounds.
It doesn't sound bad. Anxiety shows up in the stomach all the time. It's real, it's just not the flu. What was going on in your head on Saturday before you texted?
That they were like four hours away and I didn't know when they were coming back. Like they said Sunday, but what if something happened and they didn't, and I'm just stuck at my grandma's.
So the scary part is that they won't come back and you'll be stuck. That's a hard thought to sit with at your grandma's kitchen table. Zero to ten, how high was it Saturday?
Seven. Maybe higher right before I texted.
Seven. Thanks. Mom, from your side?
So I left the wedding lunch and drove back. Fifty minutes. My husband stayed. And honestly I was a little annoyed and then I felt bad about being annoyed. Anyway.
That's a really normal mix to feel. Lucia, after school. I see the library and Priya's house in the log. What's that about?
I just don't like being home by myself. Like, the house makes noises. And if someone came to the door I'd be alone.
And when you do go home before Mom?
I call her. On speaker. Until she gets home.
Sometimes that's an hour. And on Tuesdays I leave work at three now so she's not alone long.
Lucia, what number would you give coming home alone?
Five, I think. It's not as bad as the weekend.
Five. That's useful, because a five is a good place to practice. Lower than the weekend, but still real. Mom, can I ask about the date nights? You wrote she texts 'where are you' a lot.
The whole time. Every twenty minutes. And she has my location up. And then this last one she texted, what if you get in an accident and I have to deal with it. Like the police and everything.
Lucia, is that the worry when they're out? That something happens on the road and it lands on you?
Kind of. Because I'm the oldest. Mateo's eleven. So it would be me.

That's a lot of responsibility to carry in your head on a Friday night. Okay. I want to pick one thing to practice this week, and I want you to pick, Lucia, because you're fourteen and this is your plan. Option one is after school. Option two is the next time your parents go out. Which feels more doable?
After school. I guess.

Okay. Here's a version. Two days this week, you come straight home. You don't call Mom when you walk in. You set a timer for thirty minutes and do something normal. Snack, show, homework. When the timer goes off, you can text Mom one time if you want. Not a call.
Thirty minutes is a long time.
It might feel long the first time. What would be doable?
Twenty?
Twenty is good. Twenty minutes, two days this week. Which days?
Monday and Thursday. Not Tuesday, she's home early Tuesday anyway.
Perfect. Mom, your part. If she does call, and she might, you say something kind and short, like 'You've got this, I'll see you at quarter to five,' and you hang up. You don't stay on.
Okay. That's going to feel mean.
It's going to feel mean to you. To her brain it's information that she can do it. Lucia, how will you write it down?
In the app? The number before and after?

Exactly. Number when you walk in, number when the timer goes off. Mom, one more thing. You mentioned Lucia's been sleeping in your room while Jorge is traveling, and up late on her phone. We're not going to touch that this week. I'd just like you to keep writing it down, including what time she gets off her phone.
Okay. I didn't know if that was even related.

Neither do I yet. That's why I want to see it written down for a couple of weeks before we decide. So, recap. Monday and Thursday, Lucia comes straight home, no call, twenty-minute timer, one text after if she wants. Mom keeps any calls short and doesn't stay on. Lucia logs her number before and after. Mom keeps logging the nights while Jorge is away. The weekend and date nights we'll come back to.
Okay.
Thank you.
